tasks.title: listen.py --all pairs both sides by the same index because no fidelity row is loaded
tasks.source: discovered this pass reading python/listen.py:439 pair_subtunes
tasks.verify: With --all and no --from-json every row is {'file': f}, so pair_subtunes falls through to row.get('matched_subtune', sub_orig) == sub_orig and stages BOTH sides at the same index. That is correct TODAY only because 0 of 95 rows carry a differing matched_subtune -- correct by coincidence, not by construction. Done when a --all run either loads build/fidelity.json for matched_subtune when it exists, or SAYS in LISTENING.md that it paired by identity and that no row needed otherwise, so a future correspondence defect cannot silently return to staging mismatched music. A test in test_listen_all.py pins the fallback.
tasks.why_model: a bounded single-file change against an existing fallback, with the correct behaviour already decided
tasks.why_mode: one module plus its two existing tests; nothing shared has to be rebuilt
tasks.why_lane: writes python/listen.py and reads python/fidelity.py, which the search-subtunes task writes
